title: Grouping and Partitioning
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of grouping and partitioning and identify when it is appropriate in a Java program.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study grouping and partitioning with a short explanation, an original visual map, a Java example, and a check you can perform yourself. Focus on the relationship between the rule and the behavior rather than memorizing isolated syntax.
content.why_it_matters: This concept matters because it helps you compose readable data transformations and understand when stream operations execute. In this lesson, focus on groupingby() and use a minimal example to check what the rule actually guarantees.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: A stream pipeline describes transformations over a source. Intermediate operations are lazy; a terminal operation triggers work, and stream instances should not be reused after a terminal operation. The important habit is to make the assumptions explicit and use the code example as a small experiment.

items.text: A stream pipeline expresses transformations over a source. Intermediate operations are lazy, a terminal operation triggers processing, and a stream should not be reused after it is consumed. Apply that reasoning specifically to counting and summarizing grouped results and confirm the result with the example or a targeted test.
